messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: pairs() reloaded
parts:
I have now made it possible for the pairs() plot of a stanfit object to have logarithmic axes for (some) variables, the same way pairs() does for a regular matrix. It will be in the next version of rstan but you can use it now by executing

devtools::source_url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/rstan/develop/rstan/rstan/R/pairs.R")

To illustrate this with a model that samples from a bivariate Wishart distribution, you can do

Wishart <- stan_demo("wishart2x2")
pairs(Wishart, pars = c("W", "lp__"), log = TRUE, las = 1)

The log = TRUE option implies that all strictly positive variables will have logarithmic axes, or you can pass an integer vector to log. You should get something like

As you can see, there is a good deal of dependence between the covariance and each of the variances (in log units). In particular, these two planes have funnel-like shapes with larger variance at the top and lower variance at the bottom. Thus, it is difficult with a single stepsize and standard deviation of the momentum to navigate both parts of the bivariate distribution efficiently.

Ben

parts:
At the risk of sounding like Andrew, you should blog this!

In fact, what would be totally totally awesome would be
a series of posts on multivariate distributions. More people
will read it on the blog than in a paper.

The other univariate transform that would be nice to have is logit,
but that doesn't fit in directly with a log=TRUE argument. One
way to mitigate the risk of having a boolean argument is to swap
this around to scale=log, or scale=logit. Does log apply
to each variable? Or do you check the range? It'd start to get
ugly if you had to do list("W" = log, "lp__", "theta" = logit, ...).

- Bob

The png() device did work, in that it didn't hang R. Thanks. But despite your argument below, it still looks to me like there's glitch in the "log" argument results, at least for the schools example with tau. The bottom half is cut off and I don't think that should be happening. Meanwhile, your wishart example pairs plots look fine.

It looks better to the eye in this case if you make log_tau in the generated quantities block and plot that in regular scale. But I think what I said before is what is going on. There is just not enough density to the left of exp(-4) = 0.02 for it to do two-dimensional kernel density in bins. But the 128 bins it does by default cover a range of 12 in the log units better than a range of about 50 in the original units.

Ben
